scope.perCountryReport: The full report is shown for each country separately, in its own currency, because spend in different currencies is never added together. There is no combined total, no combined percentage change and no combined cost per km on this page.
scope.forecastPerCountry: The tyre forecast is shown once per country, each in its own currency. Forecast tyre counts are never added across countries, because each country is ordered and paid for separately.
scope.builderOneCountry: Charts are built one country at a time. This tool lets you put any two series on the same axis, stack them and total them, so it is only ever given one country in one currency - a chart that mixed SAR, AED and EGP would be a number that is not an amount of anything. Pick the country to chart below.
scope.builderCpkOmitted: Cost per km and cost per hour by vehicle type are left out while more than one country is in scope: those rows do not record which country they came from, so they cannot be split per country. Narrow the reporting scope to one country to chart them.

status.title: Cost status of the expense lines
status.description: Each line counted once in its own currency: actual from the ERP, estimated from the item-code median, confirmed zero (warranty), missing, or disputed (needs a person). The totals above are unchanged.
status.linesEmpty: No lines with this status in the period.

dispute.conflicting_revision: Uploaded again with a different value

hint.ACTUAL: The ERP sent an amount for this line. A negative amount is a credit (refund or return).
hint.ESTIMATED: The ERP sent no amount; the line is priced from the median of the same item code. Not a paid price.
hint.CONFIRMED_ZERO: Zero on purpose: the description marks it as warranty or free of charge.
hint.MISSING: Zero amount with no estimate and no warranty evidence. The real cost is unknown.
hint.DISPUTED: Needs a person: the same line arrived in an earlier upload, or was uploaded again with a different value.

status.disputedNote: {copyAmount} over {copyLines} lines arrived again in a later upload (the line number changed, so the import key did not catch it), and {revAmount} over {revLines} lines were uploaded again with a different value. These are still inside the total above. Nothing is removed automatically: a person decides from the lines list.
status.extrasNote: Credits (refunds and returns) {creditAmount} over {creditLines} lines. Repair lines {repairAmount} ({repairLines}), retread lines {retreadAmount} ({retreadLines}). Lines with more than one unit: {multi}.
status.loadError: Could not load the cost status.
status.notInstalled: The cost status check is not installed on this database yet.
status.pressRun: Press Run check to classify every expense line in the period. Over all dates this can take up to 15 seconds.
status.empty: No expense lines in this period.

cpk.pickCountry: Pick a single country to see money here. Each country reports in its own currency, so a combined figure would add SAR, AED and EGP together and mean nothing.
cpk.shownOnce: Over a twelve month range {prev} and the same period last year are the same dates, so they are shown once. Choose a shorter period to compare both.
cpk.withheldEarlier: The earlier period has too few odometer readings to compare against.
cpk.withheldCurrent: Not enough odometer readings in this period to measure cost per vehicle km.
cpk.withheldRule: A cost per vehicle km is only shown against a period where the measured assets cover at least {pct}% of the spend, so a change in coverage is never mistaken for a change in cost.
cpk.distanceNote: Distance comes from the odometer recorded when a tyre is fitted and when it is removed, which is the only running-kilometre data the fleet currently captures. Logging daily meter readings raises the coverage above and makes this figure fleet-wide. The tyre and maintenance split reads N/A until the database function that returns it is updated.
cpk.nothingChanged: Nothing changed between the two periods.
cpk.name: Name
cpk.weakNote: {pct}% of this spend was filed by the fallback rule, meaning nothing in the item code or description identified it. Confirming those items in Material Master moves them onto a decision rather than a guess.

variance.title: Why the cost changed
variance.blended: A change cannot be taken apart across more than one currency.
variance.notClose: The parts do not fully meet the total. The gap above is the amount the item level detail does not account for.
variance.pvNote: Price and volume are measured on the {both} item codes bought in both periods. {started} started and {stopped} stopped; those have no pair of prices to compare, so they are counted as mix rather than being given a price change that never happened.
variance.lowerBound: The final row nets many members into one figure, so movement within it can cancel out and the real total movement may be larger.
variance.noItemMoved: No item moved in this window.
variance.madeOf: What the change is made of
variance.itemsTail: A further {n} item codes moved, together {amount}.
